title: Edge policy timing flap — accountability memo and mitigation plan
content:
Purpose:
This is an accountability-style memo capturing the investigation, immediate mitigations, and a practical runbook draft for a timing-related policy evaluation flap that affected a subset of Private/VPC customers on 2026-10-05. The goal is to: 1) record what happened in plain terms, 2) propose short and medium-term mitigations, and 3) assign clear owners for follow-up work.

Summary (elevator):
On 2026-10-05 ~02:40–03:25 UTC we observed intermittent 5xx errors and connectivity timeouts from customer control-plane agents to the Private control plane for ~7 customer tenants using on-prem NAT gateways with aggressive connection tracking and short conntrack timeout settings. Root cause was a timing mismatch between edge policy evaluation TTLs (server-side cached policy validity window) and the customer NAT/timeouts — combined with a recent config roll that shortened the policy cache refresh grace interval from 60s -> 15s. The shorter grace meant that transient heartbeats aligned poorly with NAT conntrack windows, causing stateful firewall/NAT to drop inbound control-plane responses intermittently and trigger rapid reconnects, which then triggered policy reevaluation storms.

Why this is different from prior incidents: 
- Not a pure control-plane bug; it's an emergent behavior from three moving parts: our policy cache grace window, customer NAT conntrack timeouts, and a transient increase in control-plane response latency from a separate autoscaling event.
- Customer-side visibility was low: the affected customers had opaque CPE appliances and nonstandard conntrack defaults (20–40s) which amplified the problem.

Observed timeline (top-level):
- 02:35 UTC — deployment: console rollout reduced policy-cache-grace from 60s to 15s in canary (intended to make policy changes propagate faster).
- 02:40 UTC — first control-plane keepalive timeouts reported by agents for tenant cluster Z1.
- 02:45–03:00 UTC — oncall paged; initial mitigation: increased control-plane autoscaling min capacity to reduce latency (short-term).
- 03:00 UTC — correlation found between spike in policy re-evals and NAT-related TCP resets reported by customers.
- 03:10 UTC — temporary rollback of the policy-cache-grace change to previous 60s (stop-gap).
- 03:25 UTC — incident traffic subsided and metrics returned to baseline.

Key evidence and supporting logs: (snippets)
- Control-plane metric: policy_eval_rate[tenant] spiked x8 between 02:42–02:52 UTC for affected tenants.
- Agent error sample: "keepalive response timeout after 22s — retrying" from agent PID 2314.
- Customer NAT logs (redacted): multiple TCP TIME_WAIT -> RST sequences where inbound response packets were dropped due to conntrack expiry.
- Deploy timeline: console-rollout-id=rollout-2026-10-05-02:35 change: policy-cache-grace: 60 -> 15 (author: a.patel)

Hypothesis (root cause chain):
1) Policy-cache-grace reduction made server accept a narrower window for cached evaluation before forcing a re-eval on next request.
2) During a transient autoscaling-induced latency increase, some control-plane responses were delayed ~10–18s.
3) Customer NATs with conntrack timeouts of ~20s evicted the ephemeral session state during the delayed response, causing the returned control-plane packets to be dropped.
4) Dropped responses caused agents to retry and reconnect, which triggered additional immediate policy re-evaluations (because of the shorter grace window), creating a feedback spike and compounding the problem.

Immediate actions taken (what we did during incident):
- Rolled back policy-cache-grace to 60s (owner: Asha P.).
- Raised min autoscaling capacity to reduce tail latency for control-plane region (owner: SRE infra).
- Engaged customer support to request temporary adjustments to conntrack where possible (owners: CS + Solutions Eng).
- Enabled ephemeral logging for affected tenants for 1h to capture end-to-end traces (owner: Marisol T.).

Mitigations and runbook (short-term, 1–7 days):
- Runbook step: If you see simultaneous policy_eval_rate spike + agent keepalive timeouts, immediately check recent console rollouts for policy-cache parameters (command: gcloud storage cat rollout-ids | grep policy-cache-grace).
- Short-term default: enforce a minimum policy-cache-grace default of 45s for Private deployments until we complete a stability test matrix (owner: product + infra).
- Add alert rule: "policy-eval vs keepalive mismatch" composite that fires when policy_eval_rate > 3x baseline AND agent_keepalive_timeout_rate > 1% for a tenant for > 3 minutes. (owner: observability)
- Customer play: proactively contact customers with on-prem NATs and recommend conntrack >= 120s as a best-effort while we harden defaults (owner: solutions-eng).

Longer-term engineering work (30–90 days):
- Formalize grace vs latency modeling: build a simulator to test interactions of policy-cache-grace, control-plane tail latency distribution, and common conntrack defaults. Deliverable: synthetic testbench and guidance doc (owner: applied-ml / infra simulation team).
- Make policy-cache-grace an explicit tenant-level override with per-tenant safety caps (so we can revert in high-risk environments without global rollback). (owner: product + backend).
- Improve agent-side retransmission logic: add jittered backoff + detect likely conntrack expiry and request a fast reconnect policy that avoids immediate policy re-eval (owner: agents team).
- Telemetry: add conntrack-proxy heuristics to agent logs to surface probable NAT expiries (owner: agents + observability).

Runbook draft (steps for oncall):
1) Verify symptoms: check agent_keepalive_timeout, policy_eval_rate, controlplane_tail_latency.
2) Check recent rollout diffs for policy-cache-grace key. If changed in last 60m, consider immediate rollback to previous value.
3) If rollback not possible quickly: increase control-plane capacity temporarily and widen grace window via feature-flag.
4) Contact customer (if Private) to ask for conntrack bump or scheduled maintenance window.
5) Keep elevated logging for 1h; collect control-plane traces and customer NAT logs.
6) Post-incident: open JIRA with root-cause tags and schedule a triage meeting with product and solutions-eng.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did the autoscaler cause tail latency at the same time as rollout? Hypothesis: canary nodes were warming; need to review the autoscale cooldowns and warmup behavior. (owner: release-engineering)
- Are there customers with nonstandard NAT/edge appliances that we should maintain a registry for? We currently lack a centralized inventory. (owner: solutions-eng + customer-ops)
- Would a client-side keepalive redesign (probing more frequently but with lower volume) reduce sensitivity to conntrack expiry? We need an experiment. (owner: agents)

Postmortem/communication plan:
- Short internal summary to SRE, Eng Infra, Product and CS (within 24h) — owner: Marisol T.
- Customer-facing note for affected tenants describing incident, root cause, and recommended config changes (within 48h) — owner: CS lead.
- Follow-up triage with cross-functional owners to define the 30/60/90 day roadmap items above and status checkpoints.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Asha P: revert policy-cache-grace default to 60s in staging and run smoke for 48h (ETA: 2026-10-07).
- Kenji N: add composite alert rule in observability (ETA: 2026-10-08).
- Liam O'C: coordinate CS outreach to 6 known at-risk tenants and document their NAT defaults (ETA: 2026-10-12).
- Agents team (TBD): prototype conntrack-detection telemetry change (ETA: 2026-11-01).
- Release Eng: review autoscaler warmup behavior and send recommendations (ETA: 2026-10-20).

Appendix: quick commands and pointers
- Observability queries: 
  - agent_keepalive_timeout_rate: sum(rate(agent_keepalive_timeouts[5m])) by (tenant)
  - policy_eval_rate: sum(rate(policy_eval_attempts[1m])) by (tenant)
- Rollout audit: console list-rollouts --since 2026-10-05 | grep policy-cache-grace
- Slack thread: #sre-oncall 2026-10-05-controlplane-flap (contains real-time debugging notes and partial customer logs).

Notes to self / raw fragments captured during oncall: 
- "conntrack windows align badly with our 15s policy TTL — saw several TCP RST patterns in customer logs"
- "some tenants had CPE with default 30s conntrack — dangerous"
- "we should not make grace windows globally aggressive without a safety check"

If you're assigned an action above, add updates as comments in this doc and ping me in #sre-oncall. This is a working accountability memo; I'll convert to a formal postmortem if owners finish the 30/60/90 deliverables.

End of memo.
